header.running_head: The Practices of Nabi ﷺ and the Sahabah (RA) with Regard to Clothing

blocks.text: around, I saw that it was Rasulullaah ﷺ. 'O Rasulullaah ﷺ!' I said, 'It is but a simple black and white striped shawl.' Rasulullaah ﷺ replied, 'Do you not have an example in me?' When I looked at him, I saw that Rasulullaah ﷺ's garment reached halfway up his calves." [^1]
The Sahabah (RA) Describe the Attire of Rasulullaah ﷺ

Hadhrat Abu Burdah narrates that Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) once took out and showed them a patched shawl and a loincloth made of coarse cloth. She then said, "It was in these two garments that the soul of Rasulullaah ﷺ was taken away." [^2]
Hadhrat Ummu Salamah (RA) says, "The garment Rasulullaah ﷺ loved most was his Qamees[^3]." [^4]
Hadhrat Asmaa bint Yazeed (RA) reports that the sleeve of Rasulullaah ﷺ's Qamees reached his wrists.
Hadhrat Jaabir (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ was wearing a black turban when he entered Makkah the day he conquered it.
Hadhrat Amr bin Hurayth (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ once delivered a sermon wearing a black turban.
Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) says that once (during his illness) Rasulullaah ﷺ delivered a sermon while wearing an oily bandage.

Hadhrat Naafi reports from Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) that when Rasulullaah ﷺ tied his turban, he would let the tails hang between his shoulders. Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) also tied his turban in the same manner and a narrator called Abdullaah says that he saw Hadhrat Qaasim bin Muhammad and Hadhrat Saalim also do the same. [^5]
When Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) was once asked about Rasulullaah ﷺ's bedding, she replied, "It was made of leather and stuffed with the bark of a date palm." [^6]

Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) relates, "A lady from the Ansaar once visited me and saw that Rasulullaah ﷺ's bedding comprised of cloak that was double-folded. She then left and later sent a bedding stuffed with wool. When Rasulullaah ﷺ came to me, he asked, 'What is this, O Aa'isha?' I then informed him about the lady from the Ansaar who had seen his bedding and then sent this. Rasulullaah ﷺ told me to return it. Because I liked to have it in my room, I did not return it until Rasulullaah ﷺ repeated the instruction three times. He finally said, 'Return it, O Aa'isha. I swear by Allaah that if I willed, Allaah would have made mountains of
A long, loose tailored upper garment.
Bukhaari and Muslim. Ibn Sa'd (Vol.1 Pg.464) has reported a similar narration.
